clue.text: The French in charge in a secular way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective: a laic matter is handled in a secular way, not a clerical one

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A French official runs things without any religious bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic describes the lay, non-clerical side of life, the opposite of churchly or religious.

clue.text: Satirical piece of southern personal equipment

parts.note: kit is the gear a person carries, as a soldier's or sportsman's kit

explanation.surface: A send-up of the gear carried by someone from the South.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch that mocks something is a satirical piece of theatre.

clue.text: Common fund to provide bathing facility

explanation.surface: Clubbing money together to build a swimming spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Money staked jointly is a shared kitty, and a swimming bath is the other sense.

clue.text: Took up publicity briefly on dispersed depot

parts.note: an ad is short for advertisement, a piece of publicity

indicators.note: the letters of depot are scattered and regathered in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes on an advertising campaign at a scattered warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' is the anagram signal acting on 'depot', giving OPTED; 'briefly' tells you to shorten publicity's word, and 'on' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up a cause or a child is to embrace or assume it as one's own.

clue.text: A Caledonian makes a dash for it at a fashionable meeting

parts.note: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot
to make a dash is to run fast, to race

explanation.surface: A Scotsman bolts at a smart social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a racecourse near Windsor whose June races are a high point of the English social season.
explanation.definitionFit: The June horse-racing fixture near Windsor is a society event famous for fashion and hats.

clue.text: American author to raise capital in England

parts.note: to jack up a car is to raise it
London is the capital city of England

explanation.surface: A US writer trying to raise money in the English capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of The Call of the Wild was a novelist from California.

clue.text: Tom's vital statistics

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and its vital statistics are taken as the number of lives it is said to have

explanation.surface: A man named Tom's body measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat, and 'vital' points at lives rather than measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore credits a cat with surviving many brushes with death, a count of nine.

clue.text: Positively foolhardy, if comparatively edible

explanation.surface: Reckless behaviour, but tasty if taken further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positively' means in the positive degree of the adjective; the comparative form adds -ER, giving a slice of bacon you can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: In the plain degree it means reckless; its comparative form spells a bacon slice.

clue.text: Strengthen equestrian control power

parts.note: a rein is the strap a rider uses to control a horse
force means power or might

explanation.surface: A rider's grip on the horse gains muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster something is to add support to it, making it stronger.

clue.text: Beastly place to find a neat writer!

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle or oxen
a pen is an instrument for writing

explanation.surface: Somewhere awful where you would meet a tidy author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy; it is the archaic word for oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for livestock is a place where beasts are kept.

clue.text: As well to add nothing

parts.note: O, shaped like a zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Adding nothing in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Also or in addition are everyday synonyms for the phrase.

clue.text: Club for one with pressing needs

explanation.surface: A golf club for someone who has urgent requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like urgent; it is smoothing clothes, which is what the household appliance is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with an angled metal head, and the household appliance used to press laundry.

clue.text: Even poetically it's in between

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the following word

explanation.surface: A poet's version of a word lies somewhere in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: E'en is the contracted poetic spelling used in verse for this adverb.

clue.text: Satisfactory bargain to a considerable extent

explanation.surface: A fair trade, by quite some margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A good transaction is a satisfying bargain, and the phrase also means much or a lot.

clue.text: Ideal place for those kitchen sink dramas?

definitions.text: Ideal place for those kitchen sink dramas?

parts.words: Ideal place for those kitchen sink dramas?
parts.note: kitchen sink drama was gritty domestic theatre, and a kitchen garment suggests the part of a stage jutting into the audience

explanation.surface: Asking where gritty domestic plays are best staged.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink drama was 1950s British realist theatre about working-class home life; the kitchen garment names the forestage in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The forestage projecting beyond the proscenium arch is named after the cook's protective garment.

clue.text: White rose modified in a different way

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire emblem changed from its usual form.
explanation.walkthrough: The white rose is the emblem of Yorkshire; 'modified' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Done differently or by other means is the adverbial sense of the word.

clue.text: 501 + 6 = 500 concludes shareholder's profits

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
VI is the Roman numeral for six
D is the Roman numeral for 500
concludes means finishes or ends

explanation.surface: A piece of arithmetic that winds up in an investor's returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum is not meant to add up: each number is written in Roman numerals and the symbols simply join them.
explanation.definitionFit: Payouts made from a company's earnings to its stockholders are their share of profit.

clue.text: Tarsi listed on the menu

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tarsi listed on the menu', is garbled OCR: 'Tarsi' gives nothing towards FARE and no repair within three letters is evident; no reprint found.

clue.text: Storage place for Noah's bees, as the Cockney said

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H, so the two words are spoken like the record store

parts.note: Noah's vessel was an ark, and a colony of bees lives in a hive

explanation.surface: Where Noah kept his bees, in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the initial H, so ark plus hive is said ark-ive.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository for records and documents is a place for keeping things.

clue.text: Miss Gardner with risotto; there's greed for you!

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star
risotto is an Italian dish of rice

explanation.surface: A film star tucks into a large risotto, gluttonously.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive desire for wealth is a synonym for greed.

clue.text: Sure to be broken up in crate

indicators.note: something broken up is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is bound to get smashed inside a packing case.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite and confident are both synonyms for sure.

clue.text: Remarkable person; unique, surely?

explanation.surface: An exceptional individual, surely one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as one-er, something that is the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an exceptional individual, and taken as one-er it suggests something singular.

clue.text: Judges of Man

parts.note: the Isle of Man has its own legal system, whose two chief justices bear a special title

explanation.surface: Those who pass judgement on humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like mankind; it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The justices of the Isle of Man's high court carry this historic title.

clue.text: Brace soundly like 10

indicators.note: soundly says the answer is spoken the same way as the cross-referenced word

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer at 10 down

explanation.surface: A firm support that resembles another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace of birds means a pair.

clue.text: Request for a reason to be heard running into the Severn

indicators.note: to be heard means spoken, so a soundalike gives the spelling

parts.note: asking for a reason is asking why

explanation.surface: Asking why something flows into a big British river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river; its tributary rises in Wales and joins it near Chepstow.
explanation.definitionFit: The river along the Welsh border is a tributary that flows into the larger river at its estuary.

clue.text: Private tuition provides setting for such a case

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer set within its letters, like a jewel in a mount

explanation.surface: Private lessons give the backdrop for a legal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a law case; it is a small needle box.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental container for needles and sewing items is a kind of case.

clue.text: Gainful advice to the trawlerman

parts.note: a fisherman is told to catch in his mesh the earnings left after costs

explanation.surface: Tips for a fisherman on making money.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the phrase tells the trawlerman to catch with his mesh; read as an accounting term, it is earnings after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings left after all expenses are deducted, read also as an order to a fisherman.

clue.text: Storyteller turns up to scold

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: someone who tells stories is a liar

explanation.surface: A tale-teller appears to tell someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail at someone is to rant or complain bitterly at them.

clue.text: Terrible high moorland

explanation.surface: An awful stretch of upland heath.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective for fierce or cruel, and a northern English word for a hill or upland moor.

clue.text: Domesticated, small thanks to me

parts.note: ta is a short, informal word for thanks

explanation.surface: A pet is tamed, with little gratitude to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A domesticated animal is docile rather than wild.

clue.text: What did the American say about this moulding?

indicators.note: say means the exclamation is spoken, giving a soundalike

parts.note: an American exclaims oh gee in surprise

explanation.surface: Asking what a US visitor remarked about some architectural trim.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-shaped curve used as a decorative architectural moulding.

clue.text: The enlightening influence of the ghost hunter

definitions.text: The enlightening influence of the ghost hunter

parts.words: The enlightening influence of the ghost hunter
parts.note: a ghost hunter's light source is read as one fuelled by alcohol, punning on spirit as ghost

explanation.surface: A ghost hunter's illuminating impact on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' is both a ghost and methylated spirit, which fuels the lamp that gives light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp burning methylated spirit gives light, and a ghost is a spirit.
